rationale: The candidate is a small, compact mass with some non-rectangular plan interest, but across the four views it reads primarily as a boxed, two-part extrusion with a shallow notch rather than a single dominant neighborhood-building gesture. The open-space figure is weak: there is no clearly usable court, entry seam, or undercut tied to the thick blue frontage, and the access edge appears semantically underdeveloped rather than invited. The top view shows a plan split, but the perspective views do not consistently support that spatial rule, so the form is only partially coherent across views. Repair integrity is decent because the mass is not visibly broken or self-colliding, but the program fit fails because neighborhood living needs an active ground threshold and a public void/terrace relationship that this candidate does not yet establish. The references suggest that a compact civic/neighborhood mass can work when the void is explicit and the upper mass preserves a clear ground relation; here that principle is not yet achieved.
